name: Desogestrel
mechanism: Synthetic progestogen - primarily works by inhibiting ovulation (inhibits LH surge), also thickens cervical mucus and thins endometrium
dosing: Progestogen-only pill (POP): 75mcg OD continuously (no pill-free interval). Take at same time daily (12-hour window)
contraindications: Current VTE (avoid if possible, caution), current/recent breast cancer, severe liver disease, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding
interactions: Enzyme inducers (↓ effect - use additional contraception), enzyme inhibitors (possible ↑ effect)
monitoring: Review need annually. Check BP, discuss irregular bleeding patterns. Counsel on missed pill rules
pregnancy: Not known to be harmful if conception occurs. Stop when pregnancy confirmed
sideEffects: Irregular bleeding (common - may settle after 3 months), headache, acne, breast tenderness, mood changes, weight change, ovarian cysts (usually resolve)
pharmacokinetics: Rapidly absorbed, converted to active metabolite etonogestrel, half-life: 30 hours, hepatic metabolism
clinicalPearls: Only POP that reliably inhibits ovulation (>97% of cycles). More forgiving than older POPs - 12-hour window vs 3-hour. Good choice when oestrogen contraindicated (e.g. breastfeeding, migraine with aura, VTE risk). Bleeding patterns often irregular initially
indication: Contraception (especially when oestrogen contraindicated), suitable for breastfeeding women
